motivation: Community-buffering v1 showed frequent persistence of other seagrasses after exact-point Thalassia loss. This test asks whether retaining seagrass occupancy after focal loss predicts subsequent focal return, distinguishing habitat-continuity versus alternative-state lock-in patterns.

source.prerequisite: analysis/33_community_buffering.py output from pinned tbep-tech/obis-example commit 6c567beff95ea04f0e397101befb49d5233ace8f
source.point_year_state_rule: same consensus rule as community-buffering v1; within-year conflicting repeated visits excluded upstream

primary_sequence.period_rule: source year t >=2016 and recovery year t+2 <=2025
primary_sequence.t_plus_1: same point is re-observed and Thalassia absent
primary_sequence.t_plus_2: same point is re-observed exactly one year later; endpoint is Thalassia recorded present versus absent

primary_hypothesis.statement: The probability of Thalassia return at t+2 differs according to whether the t+1 loss state retained another seagrass or lost seagrass occupancy entirely.
primary_hypothesis.estimator: return fraction after other_seagrass intermediate minus return fraction after no_seagrass intermediate
primary_hypothesis.uncertainty: stable-transect node-cluster bootstrap across all eligible three-year sequences

classification.habitat_continuity: 95% bootstrap interval for difference entirely above zero

secondary_descriptive: Bay-segment-specific return fractions by intermediate class
Return fractions by identity of the t+1 alternative seagrass
Fraction of t+1 alternative taxa persisting into t+2 among Thalassia-return and non-return sequences
claim_boundary: Post-hoc derived ecological endpoint from an already-opened exact-point panel; not independent confirmation.
Return means re-recorded Thalassia at the same stable meter mark, not demographic recolonization from outside the patch.

An association between intermediate community state and return can reflect habitat filtering, residual rhizomes, local environment, or species interactions; it does not identify facilitation or competition.
Other-seagrass occupancy is not assumed to preserve equivalent ecosystem function.
Do not change the three-year sequence definition, period, intermediate classes, bootstrap unit, event/node minima, or directional classification after opening the endpoint.
